s1.text:
What changed from round 1 (direction A)

Five switches sit together in the command row, always in view: Map, Panes, Comm, Keys, and fullscreen. A lit icon is on. Comm's icon carries the unread count while Comm is hidden.

The pane box has no tabs: swipe sideways for Group, Timers, Character, Statistics. Dots show where you are.

The map has no zoom keys: pinch.

Hot keys sit above the compass, as on the phone.

Frames follow the desktop's Lykta: iron ring with rivets, hood plate, lamp-lit window, frosted cards, a glow in the gap.

s2.text:
What fills the room

Landscape: the keys share the foot of the column with the pane box. Keys hidden: the pane box takes the full width (L3). A pane switched off gives its height to the others. All three off: the column is gone and the text owns the screen, keys over its corner (L4).

Portrait: keys hidden means the command field runs the full width (P3). A pane switched off widens the other two; all three off removes the band.

s3.text:
Settled by the owner (2026-11-12)

The switches sit in the command row (X1 is not chosen). The column's order is right. In portrait the keys ride above the keyboard. Two rows of three hot keys.

s4.text:
Revision (same day)

One thick frame goes round all the panes: Map, Comm and the pane box lie in the same floating box, with hairlines between them. Pane names are quiet labels in the corner, no plates.

A divider with a grip can be dragged. Landscape: Map / Comm always; Comm / pane box only while the keys are hidden (L3), since the keys' row has a fixed height. Portrait: both dividers in the band.

In landscape the keys stand inside the frame, in their own darker cell.
